answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a falcon as the anchor of the cost.
